units.zh: 志第十五 五行三
units.en: Treatise Fifteen: The Five Elements, Part Three.
units.literal: Treatise Fifteen: The Five Elements, Part Three.

units.zh: 大水 水变色 大寒 雹 冬雷 山鸣 鱼孽 蝗
units.en: This section treats great floods, discolored water, bitter cold, hail, thunder in winter, mountains that thunder, fish omens, and locust swarms.
units.literal: Great floods; water changing color; extreme cold; hail; winter thunder; mountains roaring; fish prodigies; locusts.

units.zh: 《五行传》曰：「简宗庙，不祷祠，废祭祀，逆天时，则水不润下」谓水失其性而为灾也。
units.en: The "Treatise on the Five Elements" says: "When one slights the ancestral shrines, does not pray at the altars, abandons sacrifices, and goes against Heaven's seasons, then water fails to moisten downward"—meaning water loses its proper nature and becomes calamity.
units.literal: The "Treatise on the Five Elements" says: "When one slights the ancestral shrines, does not pray at the altars, abandons sacrifices, and goes against Heaven's seasons, then water fails to moisten downward"—meaning water loses its proper nature and becomes calamity.

units.zh: 又曰：「听之不聪，是谓不谋。
units.en: The same text adds that when the ruler "does not hear clearly," counsel goes unheard—that is the fault called "lack of planning.
units.literal: It also says: "When hearing is not keen, that is called a failure to deliberate.

units.zh: 厥咎急，厥罚恒寒，厥极贫。
units.en: The omen-chain names rash governance as the moral fault, unrelenting cold as the matching scourge, and grinding poverty as its bitter end.
units.literal: Its blame is haste; its scourge is constant cold; its utmost end is destitution.

units.zh: 时则有鼓妖，时则有鱼孽，时则有豕祸，时则有耳疴，时则有黑眚、黑祥，惟火沴水。」
units.en: Such ages bring freak drumming, fish omens, swine plagues, ear diseases, and black hauntings—while in the mutual overcoming of phases, fire is said to encroach on water."
units.literal: In such seasons there are drum prodigies, fish prodigies, pig calamities, ailments of the ear, black spectral visitations and black auspices—only fire harms water."

units.zh: 鱼孽，刘歆传以为介虫之孽，谓蝗属也。
units.en: Liu Xin's school reads "fish prodigies" alongside omens among armored or shelled vermin—in practice, the locust plague.
units.literal: Fish prodigies"—Liu Xin's tradition classes them with omens among shelled creatures, meaning the locust kind.

units.zh: 和帝永元元年七月，郡国九大水，伤稼。
units.en: Yongyuan 1 (89 CE), seventh month: nine provinces were inundated and the standing grain was ruined.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Yongyuan, Emperor He, nine commanderies and kingdoms suffered great floods that injured the crops.

units.zh: 京房《易传》曰：「颛事有知，诛罚绝理，厥灾水。
units.en: Jing Fang's "Tradition of the Changes" says: "When one monopolizes affairs with cunning knowledge, and punishments and executions cut off what is right, the calamity is flood.
units.literal: Jing Fang's "Tradition of the Changes" says: "When one monopolizes affairs with cunning knowledge, and punishments and executions cut off what is right, the calamity is flood.

units.zh: 其水也，雨杀人，陨霜，大风，天黄。
units.en: The portents cluster: lethal downpours, untimely frost, howling gales, and a sallow, yellowed sky.
units.literal: As for that flood: rain kills people; frost falls; great winds; the sky turns yellow.

units.zh: 饥而不损，兹谓泰，厥水水杀人。
units.en: When hunger stalks the land yet the court refuses relief—false "tranquility"—the waters rise until they carry off the people.
units.literal: Famine yet no reduction—this is called "great peace"; its flood is flood that kills people.

units.zh: 辟遏有德，兹谓狂，厥水水流杀人，已水则地生虫。
units.en: To bar worthy men from office is the madness of policy; rivers then run wild and, when they withdraw, leave the fields worm-ridden.
units.literal: Blocking and thwarting the virtuous—this is called madness; its flood is flowing water that kills people, and after the water recedes the ground breeds worms.

units.zh: 归狱不解，兹谓追非，厥水寒杀人。
units.en: When the innocent languish in jail, the omen is killing cold carried on the flood.
units.literal: Cases left in prison without release—this is called pursuing what is wrong; its flood is cold water that kills people.

units.zh: 追诛不解，兹谓不理，厥水五谷不收。
units.en: Endless vindictive killing is "disorder"; the harvest fails and the granaries stand empty.
units.literal: Pursuing executions without release—this is called lack of order; its flood is the five grains not gathered.

units.zh: 大败不解，兹谓皆阴，厥水流入国邑，陨霜杀谷。」
units.en: When a shattering military reverse is never redressed—total yin dominance—rivers invade the cities and late frost finishes the crops."
units.literal: Great defeat without release—this is called all yin; its flood flows into the capital and towns, frost falls and kills the grain.

units.zh: 是时，和帝幼，窦太后摄政，其兄窦宪干事，及宪诸弟皆贵显，并作威虣虐，尝所怨恨，辄任客杀之。
units.en: The emperor was a child; Dou Xian and his kin ran the realm from behind the dowager's screen, swaggering in rank and murdering scores by private assassins whenever spite moved them.
units.literal: At that time Emperor He was young; Empress Dowager Dou held the government; her brother Dou Xian managed affairs, and Xian and his brothers were all noble and prominent, together acting fierce and cruel; whenever they nursed a grudge they would at once employ retainers to murder the object.

units.zh: 其后窦氏诛灭。
units.en: In time the whole Dou faction was swept away and put to the sword.
units.literal: Afterward the Dou clan was executed and extinguished.

units.zh: 十二年六月，颍川大水，伤稼。
units.en: Yongyuan 12 (100 CE), sixth month: the Yingchuan plain went under and the harvest was lost.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year, Yingchuan suffered a great flood that injured the crops.

units.zh: 是时，和帝幸邓贵人，阴有欲废阴后之意，阴后亦怀恚怨。
units.en: The court had turned to Lady Deng while Empress Yin, sensing she would be cast off, nursed a bitter grudge.
units.literal: At that time Emperor He favored Worthy Lady Deng and secretly intended to depose Empress Yin; the empress also harbored resentment.

units.zh: 一曰，先是恭怀皇后葬礼有阙，窦太后崩后，乃改殡梁后，葬西陵，征舅三人皆为列侯，位特进，赏赐累千金。
units.en: Another gloss ties the flood to the shabby obsequies for Empress Gonghuai, the belated reinterment of Empress Liang at Xiling after Dou's death, and the sudden enrichment of three uncles at the highest noble rank.
units.literal: One view says: earlier the funeral rites for Empress Gonghuai had been deficient; after Empress Dowager Dou died, they reburied Empress Liang in the west mausoleum and summoned three maternal uncles, all enfeoffed as marquises with special-advance rank, gifts mounting to a thousand catties of gold.

units.zh: 殇帝延平元年五月，郡国三十七大水，伤稼。
units.en: Yanping 1 (106 CE), fifth month: thirty-seven provinces flooded and the fields were battered.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yanping, Emperor Shang, thirty-seven commanderies and kingdoms suffered great floods that injured the crops.

units.zh: 董仲舒曰：「水者，阴气盛也。」
units.en: Dong Zhongshu said: "Water means yin qi is abundant."
units.literal: Dong Zhongshu said: "Water means yin qi is abundant."

units.zh: 是时，帝在襁抱，邓太后专政。
units.en: The boy on the throne was still in arms; Empress Dowager Deng held every rein of power.
units.literal: At that time the emperor was in swaddling clothes; Empress Dowager Deng monopolized government.

units.zh: 安帝永初元年冬十月辛酉，河南新城山水虣出，突坏民田，坏处泉水出，深三丈。
units.en: Yongchu 1 (107 CE), late autumn: a flash flood out of the Xincheng hills in Henan tore through farmland, and new springs welled ten yards deep in the scour.
units.literal: In the winter, tenth month, on the day xinyou of the first year of Yongchu, Emperor An, mountains and rivers in Xincheng, Henan, burst forth violently, smashed private fields, and where they broke open springs gushed up three zhang deep.

units.zh: 是时司空周章等以邓太后不立皇太子胜而立清河王子，故谋欲废置。
units.en: Zhou Zhang and his fellow ministers resented the dowager's choice of the Qinghe infant over Prince Sheng and conspired to reverse the succession.
units.literal: At that time Minister of Works Zhou Zhang and others, because Empress Dowager Deng had not enthroned Heir Apparent Sheng but the son of the Prince of Qinghe, therefore plotted to depose and replace.

units.zh: 十一月，事觉，章等被诛。
units.en: Eleventh month: the plot leaked; Zhou Zhang and his allies went to the block.
units.literal: In the eleventh month the affair was discovered; Zhang and the others were executed.

units.zh: 是年郡国四十一水出，漂没民人。
units.en: That same year forty-one jurisdictions saw rivers overrun their banks and sweep away whole communities.
units.literal: That year forty-one commanderies and kingdoms had water break out, drifting away and drowning the people.

units.zh: 《谶》曰：「水者，纯阴之精也。
units.en: The "Chen" prophecy says: "Water is the essence of pure yin.
units.literal: The "Chen" prophecy says: "Water is the essence of pure yin.

units.zh: 阴气盛洋溢者，小人专制擅权，妒疾贤者，依公结私，侵乘君子，小人席胜，失怀得志，故涌水为灾。」
units.en: When yin swells past measure, mean men seize the levers of state, envy the good, trade on public trust for private gain, and trample their betters—so the rivers boil up in answer."
units.literal: When yin qi flourishes and overflows, petty men monopolize power, are jealous of the worthy, rely on public office to pursue private ends, encroach upon gentlemen; petty men sit atop victory, lose restraint and get their will—therefore surging water becomes calamity."

units.zh: 二年，大水。
units.en: Yongchu 2: another year of widespread flooding.
units.literal: The second year: great flood.

units.zh: 三年，大水。
units.en: Yongchu 3: floods again.
units.literal: The third year: great flood.

units.zh: 四年，大水。
units.en: Yongchu 4: the inundations continued.
units.literal: The fourth year: great flood.

units.zh: 五年，大水。
units.en: Yongchu 5: still the rivers would not stay their banks.
units.literal: The fifth year: great flood.

units.zh: 六年，河东池水变色，皆赤如血。
units.en: Yongchu 6: the ponds of Hedong turned the color of blood.
units.literal: In the sixth year the pools of Hedong changed color, all red as blood.

units.zh: 是时，邓太后犹专政。
units.en: The dowager's regency still gripped the court.
units.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Deng still monopolized government.

units.zh: 延光三年，大水，流杀民人，伤苗稼。
units.en: Yanguang 3 (124 CE): catastrophic freshets drowned people and laid waste to the young grain.
units.literal: In the third year of Yanguang there was a great flood; flowing water killed the people and injured the seedling crops.

units.zh: 是时安帝信江京、樊丰及阿母王圣等谗言，免太尉杨震，废皇太子。
units.en: The emperor listened to his eunuchs and his wet nurse, cashiered Yang Zhen, and cast down the crown prince—classic signs of a tottering house.
units.literal: At that time Emperor An believed the slander of Jiang Jing, Fan Feng, and his nurse Wang Sheng and the like, dismissed Grand Commandant Yang Zhen, and deposed the heir apparent.

units.zh: 质帝本初元年五月，海水溢乐安、北海，溺杀人、物。
units.en: Benchu 1 (146 CE), fifth month: the Bohai tide surged into Le'an and Beihai, swallowing lives and property.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Benchu, Emperor Zhi, the sea overflowed Le'an and Beihai, drowning people and goods.

units.zh: 是时帝幼，梁太后专政。
units.en: Another child emperor; the Liang empress dowager held the regency.
units.literal: At that time the emperor was young; Empress Dowager Liang monopolized government.

units.zh: 桓帝建和二年七月，京师大水。
units.en: Jianhe 2 (148 CE), seventh month: Luoyang was awash.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Jianhe, Emperor Huan, the capital suffered a great flood.

units.zh: 去年冬，梁冀枉杀故太尉李固、杜乔。
units.en: Only months after Liang Ji had framed and executed the two grand commandants Li Gu and Du Qiao.
units.literal: The previous winter Liang Ji had unjustly killed the former Grand Commandants Li Gu and Du Qiao.

units.zh: 三年八月，京都大水。
units.en: Jianhe 3, eighth month: the capital flooded again.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the third year the capital suffered a great flood.

units.zh: 是时，梁太后犹专政。
units.en: The Liang dowager still pulled every string from behind the curtain.
units.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Liang still monopolized government.

units.zh: 永兴元年秋，河水溢，漂害人、物。
units.en: Yongxing 1 (153 CE), autumn: the great river burst its dikes and carried off people and stores.
units.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Yongxing the Yellow River overflowed, drifting away and injuring people and goods.

units.zh: 二年六月，彭城泗水增长，逆流。
units.en: Yongxing 2, sixth month: the Si swelled so violently at Pengcheng that it ran upstream.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the second year the Si River in Pengcheng rose and flowed backward.

units.zh: 永寿元年六月，雒水溢至津阳城门，漂流人、物。
units.en: Yongshou 1 (155 CE), sixth month: the Luo climbed to the Jinyang gate, rafting debris and bodies through the streets.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Yongshou the Luo River overflowed to the Jinyang city gate, drifting away people and goods.

units.zh: 是时梁皇后兄冀秉政，疾害忠直，威权震主。
units.en: Liang Ji, the empress's brother, dominated the bureaucracy, hunted the outspoken, and terrified even the throne.
units.literal: At that time Empress Liang's brother Ji held power, hated and injured the loyal and straight, and his awesomeness shook the ruler.

units.zh: 後遂誅滅。
units.en: He and his clan were extirpated not long after.
units.literal: Afterward he was executed and extinguished.

units.zh: 延熹八年四月，济北河水清。
units.en: Yanxi 8 (165 CE), fourth month: the Ji-north reach of the Yellow River ran transparent—a freak omen.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year of Yanxi the Yellow River in Jibei ran clear.

units.zh: 九年四月，济阴、东郡、济北、平原河水清。
units.en: Next year's fourth month: the same uncanny clarity appeared along the Yellow River in four commanderies.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year Jiyin, Dongjun, Jibei, and Pingyuan Yellow River water ran clear.

units.zh: 襄楷上言：「河者诸侯之象，清者阳明之征，岂独诸侯有规京都计邪？」
units.en: Xiang Kai submitted a memorial: "The river is the image of the feudal lords; clarity is the sign of yang brightness—does it mean only that the lords are taking aim at the capital's plans?"
units.literal: Xiang Kai submitted a memorial: "The river is the image of the feudal lords; clarity is the sign of yang brightness—does it mean only that the lords are taking aim at the capital's plans?"

units.zh: 其明年，宫车晏驾，征解犊亭侯为汉嗣，即尊位，是为孝灵皇帝。
units.en: The following year Huan died without issue; the court fetched Liu Hong, marquis of Jieduting, who ascended as Emperor Ling.
units.literal: The next year the imperial carriage delayed; the Marquis of Jieduting was summoned to continue Han; he assumed the supreme position—this was Emperor Ling.

units.zh: 永康元年八月，六州大水，勃海海溢，没杀人。
units.en: Yongkang 1 (167 CE), eighth month: six provinces drowned; the Bohai tide rolled inland and killed many.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yongkang six provinces suffered great floods; the Bohai sea overflowed and drowned people.

units.zh: 是时，桓帝奢侈淫祀，其十一月崩，无嗣。
units.en: Huan had bankrupted the treasury on shrines and pleasures; he died childless that winter.
units.literal: At that time Emperor Huan practiced extravagance and wanton sacrifice; in the eleventh month he died without heir.

units.zh: 灵帝建宁四年二月，河水清。
units.en: Jianning 4 (171 CE), second month: again the Yellow River ran crystal-clear.
units.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Jianning, Emperor Ling, the Yellow River ran clear.

units.zh: 五月，山水大出，漂坏庐舍五百余家。
units.en: Fifth month: mountain torrents smashed over five hundred dwellings.
units.literal: In the fifth month mountains and rivers burst forth greatly, drifting away and destroying more than five hundred homes.

units.zh: 熹平二年六月，东莱、北海海水溢出，漂没人物。
units.en: Xiping 2 (173 CE), sixth month: the sea breached Donglai and Beihai, wiping out lives and goods.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Xiping Donglai and Beihai sea water overflowed, drifting away and drowning people and goods.

units.zh: 三年秋，雒水出。
units.en: Xiping 3, autumn: the Luo left its channel.
units.literal: In the autumn of the third year the Luo River came out.

units.zh: 四年夏，郡国三水，伤害秋稼。
units.en: Xiping 4, summer: three jurisdictions flooded and the late-season grain was spoiled.
units.literal: In the summer of the fourth year three commanderies and kingdoms had flood; it injured the autumn crops.

units.zh: 光和六年秋，金城河溢，水出二十余里。
units.en: Guanghe 6 (183 CE), autumn: the Jincheng reach of the Yellow River spread miles beyond its banks.
units.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year of Guanghe the Jinzhou Yellow River overflowed; water came out more than twenty li.

units.zh: 中平五年，郡国六水大出。
units.en: Zhongping 5 (188 CE): six provinces were hit by major cloudbursts and river bursts.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Zhongping six commanderies and kingdoms had water break out greatly.

units.zh: 献帝建安二年九月，汉水流，害民人。
units.en: Jian'an 2 (197 CE), ninth month: the Han River rampaged through settled country.
units.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Jian'an, Emperor Xian, the Han River flowed, injuring the people.

units.zh: 是时，天下大乱。
units.en: The realm was already torn by warlord strife.
units.literal: At that time all under Heaven was in great chaos.

units.zh: 十八年六月，大水。
units.en: Jian'an 18, sixth month: another great inundation.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the eighteenth year: great flood.

units.zh: 二十四年八月，汉水溢流，害民人。
units.en: Jian'an 24, eighth month: the Han rose again and drowned communities along its course.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year the Han River overflowed and flowed, injuring the people.

units.zh: 庶征之恒寒。
units.en: Under the heading of miscellaneous portents comes unseasonable, enduring cold.
units.literal: Among the "Various Signs"—constant cold.

units.zh: 灵帝光和六年冬，大寒，北海、东莱、琅邪井中冰厚尺余。
units.en: Guanghe 6, winter: a killing frost gripped the coast—wells in Beihai, Donglai, and Langye froze over a foot thick.
units.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of Guanghe, Emperor Ling, extreme cold; in Beihai, Donglai, and Langye ice in the wells was more than a chi thick.

units.zh: 献帝初平四年六月，寒风如冬时。
units.en: Chuping 4 (193 CE), sixth month: a blast swept the land as bitter as mid-winter.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Chuping, Emperor Xian, cold wind as in wintertime.

units.zh: 和帝永元五年六月，郡国三雨雹，大如鸡子。
units.en: Yongyuan 5 (93 CE), sixth month: hailstones the size of eggs fell across three provinces.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Yongyuan, Emperor He, three commanderies and kingdoms rained hail as large as chicken eggs.

units.zh: 是时和帝用酷吏周纡为司隶校尉，刑诛深刻。
units.en: He had put the notorious Zhou Xu in charge of the capital corps; torture and summary execution became the norm.
units.literal: At that time Emperor He employed the cruel official Zhou Xu as Metropolitan Superintendent; punishments and executions were deep and severe.

units.zh: 安帝永初元年，雨雹。
units.en: Yongchu 1: hailstorms swept the north.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongchu, Emperor An: it rained hail.

units.zh: 二年，雨雹，大如鸡子。
units.en: Yongchu 2: egg-sized hail returned.
units.literal: The second year: it rained hail, large as chicken eggs.

units.zh: 三年，雨雹，大如雁子，伤稼。
units.en: Yongchu 3: hail as big as goose eggs beat down the standing grain.
units.literal: The third year: it rained hail, large as goose eggs, injuring the crops.

units.zh: 劉向以爲雹，陰脅陽也。
units.en: Liu Xiang read hail as yin force lashing out at yang.
units.literal: Liu Xiang held that hail means yin threatening yang.

units.zh: 是时邓太后以阴专阳政。
units.en: A woman regent, in Liu Xiang's cosmology, was yin ruling in yang's place.
units.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Deng used yin to monopolize yang's government.

units.zh: 元初四年六月戊辰，郡国三雨雹，大如杅杯及鸡子，杀六畜。
units.en: Yuanchu 4 (117 CE), sixth month, wuchen: three provinces were pelted with hail between cup- and egg-size; herds died in the fields.
units.literal: On the day wuchen in the sixth month of the fourth year of Yuanchu three commanderies and kingdoms rained hail, large as pestle-cups and chicken eggs, killing the six kinds of livestock.

units.zh: 延光元年四月，郡国二十一雨雹，大如鸡子，伤稼。
units.en: Yanguang 1 (122 CE), fourth month: twenty-one jurisdictions caught egg-sized hail that shredded the crops.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yanguang twenty-one commanderies and kingdoms rained hail, large as chicken eggs, injuring the crops.

units.zh: 是时安帝信谗，无辜死者多。
units.en: The emperor again lent his ear to informers; innocents perished wholesale.
units.literal: At that time Emperor An believed slander; many died without guilt.

units.zh: 三年，雨雹，大如鸡子。
units.en: Yanguang 3: another season of egg-sized hail.
units.literal: The third year: it rained hail, large as chicken eggs.

units.zh: 桓帝延熹四年五月己卯，京都雨雹，大如鸡子。
units.en: Yanxi 4 (161 CE), fifth month, jimao: Luoyang was bombarded with hail as large as eggs.
units.literal: On the day jimao in the fifth month of the fourth year of Yanxi, Emperor Huan, the capital rained hail, large as chicken eggs.

units.zh: 是时，桓帝诛杀过差，又宠小人。
units.en: Huan was slaughtering beyond measure while showering favor on sycophants.
units.literal: At that time Emperor Huan's executions exceeded what was right, and he also favored petty men.

units.zh: 七年五月己丑，京都雨雹。
units.en: Yanxi 7 (164 CE), fifth month, jichou: the capital hailstorm returned.
units.literal: On the day jichou in the fifth month of the seventh year the capital rained hail.

units.zh: 是时，皇后邓氏僭侈，骄恣专幸。
units.en: Empress Deng had grown haughty, extravagant, and jealous of every rival for the emperor's eye.
units.literal: At that time Empress Deng acted beyond her rank, was arrogant and unrestrained, and monopolized favor.

units.zh: 明年废，以忧死，其家皆诛。
units.en: The following year she was cast down, broken-hearted, and her kin extirpated.
units.literal: The next year she was deposed, died of grief, and her family were all executed.

units.zh: 灵帝建宁二年四月，雨雹。
units.en: Jianning 2 (169 CE), fourth month: hail.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Jianning, Emperor Ling: it rained hail.

units.zh: 四年五月，河东雨雹。
units.en: Jianning 4, fifth month: Hedong was hail-struck.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year Hedong rained hail.

units.zh: 光和四年六月，雨雹，大如鸡子。
units.en: Guanghe 4 (181 CE), sixth month: egg-sized hail again.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Guanghe it rained hail, large as chicken eggs.

units.zh: 是时，常侍、黄门用权。
units.en: The palace eunuchs held the real authority.
units.literal: At that time the regular attendants and Yellow Gates employed power.

units.zh: 中平二年四月庚戌，雨雹，伤稼。
units.en: Zhongping 2 (185 CE), fourth month, gengxu: hail ruined the spring planting.
units.literal: On the day gengxu in the fourth month of the second year of Zhongping it rained hail, injuring the crops.

units.zh: 献帝初平四年六月，右扶风雹如斗。
units.en: Chuping 4, sixth month: west of the capital, hail fell in lumps the size of peck measures.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Chuping, Emperor Xian, in Youfufeng hail like dou measures.

units.zh: 和帝元兴元年冬十一月壬午，郡国四冬雷。
units.en: Yuanxing 1 (105 CE), eleventh month, renwu: thunder rolled in winter across four provinces—an uncanny sound.
units.literal: On the day renwu in the eleventh month of the winter of the first year of Yuanxing, Emperor He, four commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.

units.zh: 是时皇子数不遂，皆隐之民间。
units.en: Several imperial infants had died in secret; the court hid the losses from the realm.
units.literal: At that time imperial sons repeatedly did not succeed; all were hidden among the common people.

units.zh: 是岁，宫车晏驾，殇帝生百余日，立以为君；
units.en: When He died that year the throne passed to the hundred-day-old Shang;
units.literal: That year the imperial carriage delayed; Emperor Shang, born a hundred-odd days, was set up as lord;

units.zh: 帝兄有疾，封为平原王，卒，皆夭无嗣。
units.en: the sick elder prince of Pingyuan followed him to the grave—He's line seemed cursed to die young and heirless.
units.literal: the emperor's elder brother was ill, enfeoffed as prince of Pingyuan, died—all were young without posterity.

units.zh: 殇帝延平元年九月乙亥，陈留雷，有石陨地四。
units.en: Yanping 1, ninth month, yihai: thunder over Chenliu shook four stones from the sky.
units.literal: In the ninth month on the day yihai of the first year of Yanping, Emperor Shang, Chenliu thundered, and stones fell to the ground—four.

units.zh: 安帝永初六年十月丙戌，郡六冬雷。
units.en: Yongchu 6 (112 CE), tenth month, bingxu: winter thunder in six commanderies.
units.literal: On the day bingxu in the tenth month of the sixth year of Yongchu, Emperor An, six commanderies had winter thunder.

units.zh: 七年十月戊子，郡国三冬雷。
units.en: Yongchu 7, tenth month, wuzi: three more provinces heard thunder in the dead of winter.
units.literal: On the day wuzi in the tenth month of the seventh year three commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.

units.zh: 元初元年十月癸巳，郡国三冬雷。
units.en: Yuanchu 1 (114 CE), tenth month, guisi: triple winter thunder omen.
units.literal: On the day guisi in the tenth month of the first year of Yuanchu three commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.

units.zh: 三年十月辛亥，汝南、乐浪冬雷。
units.en: Yuanchu 3, tenth month, xinhai: Ru'nan and Lelang echoed with winter peals.
units.literal: On the day xinhai in the tenth month of the third year Ru'nan and Lelang had winter thunder.

units.zh: 四年十月辛酉，郡国五冬雷。
units.en: Yuanchu 4, tenth month, xinyou: five jurisdictions lit up with off-season thunder.
units.literal: On the day xinyou in the tenth month of the fourth year five commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.

units.zh: 六年十月丙子，郡国五冬雷。
units.en: Yuanchu 6 (119 CE), tenth month, bingzi: winter thunder rolled across five provinces.
units.literal: On the day bingzi in the tenth month of the sixth year five commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.

units.zh: 永宁元年十月，郡国七冬雷。
units.en: Yongning 1 (120 CE), tenth month: seven jurisdictions heard thunder out of season.
units.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongning seven commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.

units.zh: 建光元年十月，郡国七冬雷。
units.en: Jianguang 1 (121 CE), tenth month: the same omen struck seven provinces again.
units.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Jianguang seven commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.

units.zh: 延光四年，郡国十九冬雷。
units.en: Yanguang 4 (125 CE): nineteen commanderies reported winter thunder—a widespread sign.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Yanguang nineteen commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.

units.zh: 是时，太后摄政，上无所与。
units.en: The dowager regent ran every decision; the sovereign had no voice in affairs.
units.literal: At that time the empress dowager held the government; the emperor participated in nothing.

units.zh: 太后既崩，阿母王圣及皇后兄阎显兄弟更秉威权，上遂不亲万机，从容宽仁任臣下。
units.en: When she died, the emperor's wet nurse Wang Sheng and Empress Yan's brothers seized the reins; the ruler withdrew from the daily grind of government, indulged a reputation for mildness, and left policy to his officials.
units.literal: After the empress dowager died, the nurse Wang Sheng and the empress's elder brothers Yan Xian and company in turn grasped awesome power; the emperor thereupon did not personally attend to the myriad threads of state, but was easygoing, lenient, and entrusted things to his ministers.

units.zh: 桓帝建和三年六月乙卯，雷震宪陵寝屋。
units.en: Jianhe 3 (149 CE), sixth month, yimao: lightning shattered the roof of the tomb hall at Emperor Zhang's Xianling.
units.literal: On the day yimao in the sixth month of the third year of Jianhe, Emperor Huan, thunder struck the roof of the sleeping hall at Xian Mausoleum.

units.zh: 先是梁太后听兄冀枉杀李固、杜乔。
units.en: The bolt answered Liang Ji's earlier murder of Grand Commandants Li Gu and Du Qiao at his sister's behest.
units.literal: Earlier Empress Dowager Liang had listened to her brother Ji and unjustly killed Li Gu and Du Qiao.

units.zh: 灵帝熹平六年冬十月，东莱冬雷。
units.en: Xiping 6 (177 CE), winter: thunder rolled over Donglai though snow should have sealed the sky.
units.literal: In the winter tenth month of the sixth year of Xiping, Emperor Ling, Donglai had winter thunder.

units.zh: 中平四年十二月晦，雨水，大雷电。
units.en: Zhongping 4 (187 CE), month's end: warm rain fell with deafening thunder—freak weather for deep winter.
units.literal: On the last day of the twelfth month of the fourth year of Zhongping there was rain water, great thunder and lightning.

units.zh: 雹。
units.en: Hail followed—a further portent in the same season.
units.literal: Hail.

units.zh: 献帝初平三年五月丙申，无云而雷。
units.en: Chuping 3 (192 CE), fifth month, bingshen: thunder pealed from a clear sky.
units.literal: On the day bingshen in the fifth month of the third year of Chuping, Emperor Xian, there was thunder though no clouds.

units.zh: 四年五月癸酉，无云而雷。
units.en: Chuping 4, fifth month, guiyou: again thunder without a cloud in sight.
units.literal: On the day guiyou in the fifth month of the fourth year there was thunder though no clouds.

units.zh: 建安七八年中，长沙醴陵县有大山，常大鸣如牛呴声，积数年。
units.en: Between Jian'an 7 and 8 (202–203 CE) a peak above Liling in Changsha lowed like a bull for years on end.
units.literal: In the seventh and eighth years of Jian'an there was a great mountain in Liling county, Changsha, which often roared greatly like the sound of an ox lowing, accumulating for several years.

units.zh: 后豫章贼攻没醴陵县，杀略吏民。
units.en: Then bandits from Yuzhang stormed Liling, slaughtering and looting the county.
units.literal: Afterward Yuzhang bandits attacked and overran Liling county, killing and plundering officials and people.

units.zh: 灵帝熹平二年，东莱海出大鱼二枚，长八九丈，高二丈余。
units.en: Xiping 2 (173 CE): two leviathans surfaced off Donglai—ninety feet long and twenty feet out of the water.
units.literal: In the second year of Xiping, Emperor Ling, two great fish came forth from the sea at Donglai, eight or nine zhang in length and more than two zhang in height.

units.zh: 明年，中山王暢、任城王博并薨。
units.en: The following year two imperial princes, Chang of Zhongshan and Bo of Rencheng, died the same year.
units.literal: The next year the prince of Zhongshan, Chang, and the prince of Rencheng, Bo, both died.

units.zh: 和帝永元四年，蝗。
units.en: Yongyuan 4 (92 CE): locust clouds darkened the fields.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Yongyuan, Emperor He: locusts.

units.zh: 八年五月，河内、陈留蝗。
units.en: Yongyuan 8, fifth month: the pests devoured Henei and Chenliu.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year Henei and Chenliu had locusts.

units.zh: 九月，京都蝗。
units.en: Ninth month: the swarm reached Luoyang itself.
units.literal: In the ninth month the capital had locusts.

units.zh: 九年，蝗從夏至秋。
units.en: Yongyuan 9: the infestation lasted from midsummer into fall.
units.literal: In the ninth year locusts ran from summer through autumn.

units.zh: 先是，西羌數反，遣將軍將北軍五校征之。
units.en: For years the Western Qiang had risen in revolt, drawing expedition after expedition from the capital legions.
units.literal: Earlier the Western Qiang had repeatedly rebelled; generals were dispatched with the Northern Army's five camps to chastise them.

units.zh: 安帝永初四年夏，蝗。
units.en: Yongchu 4 (110 CE), summer: locusts again.
units.literal: In the summer of the fourth year of Yongchu, Emperor An: locusts.

units.zh: 是时，西羌寇乱，军众征距，连十余年。
units.en: The Qiang war had dragged on for over a decade of campaigning.
units.literal: At that time the Western Qiang raided and threw the frontier into turmoil; armies marched and countermarched for more than ten years linked together.

units.zh: 五年夏，九州蝗。
units.en: Yongchu 5, summer: the plague of locusts spread across all nine provinces.
units.literal: In the fifth year summer the nine provinces had locusts.

units.zh: 六年三月，去蝗处复蝗子生。
units.en: Yongchu 6, third month: the stripped fields hatched a second brood of hoppers.
units.literal: In the third month of the sixth year where the locusts had gone locust larvae were born again.

units.zh: 七年夏，蝗。
units.en: Yongchu 7, summer: another wave of locusts.
units.literal: In the seventh year summer: locusts.

units.zh: 元初元年夏，郡国五蝗。
units.en: Yuanchu 1 (114 CE), summer: five commanderies were stripped bare.
units.literal: In the summer of the first year of Yuanchu five commanderies and kingdoms had locusts.

units.zh: 二年夏，郡国二十蝗。
units.en: Yuanchu 2, summer: twenty jurisdictions reported swarms.
units.literal: In the second year summer twenty commanderies and kingdoms had locusts.

units.zh: 延光元年六月，郡国蝗。
units.en: Yanguang 1 (122 CE), sixth month: a general locust plague.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Yanguang commanderies and kingdoms had locusts.

units.zh: 顺帝永建五年，郡国十二蝗。
units.en: Yongjian 5 (130 CE): twelve provinces suffered locusts.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Yongjian, Emperor Shun, twelve commanderies and kingdoms had locusts.

units.zh: 是时，鲜卑寇朔方，用众征之。
units.en: The Xianbei were probing Shuofang; the court sent a punitive host north.
units.literal: At that time the Xianbei raided Shuofang; troops were mobilized to chastise them.

units.zh: 永和元年秋七月。
units.en: Yonghe 1 (136 CE), late summer heading into autumn—the seventh month.
units.literal: Yonghe 1: the seventh month of autumn.

units.zh: 偃师蝗。
units.en: Locusts fell on Yanshi east of the capital.
units.literal: Yanshi had locusts.

units.zh: 去年冬，乌桓寇沙南，用众征之。
units.en: That followed a winter campaign against Wuhuan incursions south of the desert.
units.literal: The previous winter the Wuhuan had raided Shanan; troops were mobilized to chastise them.

units.zh: 桓帝永兴元年七月，郡国三十二蝗。
units.en: Yongxing 1 (153 CE), seventh month: thirty-two commanderies writhed under locusts.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Yongxing, Emperor Huan, thirty-two commanderies and kingdoms had locusts.

units.zh: 是时，梁冀秉政无谋宪，苟贪权作虐。
units.en: Liang Ji ruled with no respect for law or counsel—only a cruel grip on power.
units.literal: At that time Liang Ji held power without regard for fundamental norms, greedily grasping authority and committing cruelties.

units.zh: 二年六月，京都蝗。
units.en: Yongxing 2, sixth month: the capital itself was swarmed.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the second year the capital had locusts.

units.zh: 永寿三年六月，京都蝗。
units.en: Yongshou 3 (157 CE), sixth month: Luoyang again under locusts.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Yongshou the capital had locusts.

units.zh: 延熹元年五月，京都蝗。
units.en: Yanxi 1 (158 CE), fifth month: another locust year in the capital.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yanxi the capital had locusts.

units.zh: 灵帝熹平六年夏，七州蝗。
units.en: Xiping 6 (177 CE), summer: seven provinces were eaten bare.
units.literal: In the summer of the sixth year of Xiping seven provinces had locusts.

units.zh: 先是，鮮卑前後三十餘犯塞。
units.en: The Xianbei had raided the passes over thirty times running.
units.literal: Earlier the Xianbei had violated the frontier more than thirty times in succession.

units.zh: 是岁，护乌桓校尉夏育、破鲜卑中郎将田晏、使匈奴中郎将臧旻将南单于以下，三道并出讨鲜卑。
units.en: The court launched a three-pronged expedition—Xia Yu, Tian Yan, and Zang Min at the head of Wuhuan auxiliaries, Southern Xiongnu allies, and frontier garrisons—to crush the Xianbei.
units.literal: That year the Colonel Protecting the Wuhuan Xia Yu, the Gentleman-General Breaking the Xianbei Tian Yan, and the Gentleman-General Commissioner over the Xiongnu Zang Min, leading the Southern Shanyu and those below, set out on three routes together to punish the Xianbei.

units.zh: 大司农经用不足，殷敛郡国，以给军粮。
units.en: The treasury ran dry; ministers squeezed every commandery for grain to feed the armies.
units.literal: The Grand Minister of Agriculture's regular funds were insufficient; he pressed levies on commanderies and kingdoms to supply military grain.

units.zh: 三将无功，还者少半。
units.en: The campaign failed; fewer than half the men came back.
units.literal: The three generals achieved no success; of those who returned fewer than half.

units.zh: 光和元年诏策问曰：「连年蝗虫至冬踊，其咎焉在？」
units.en: Guanghe 1 (178 CE): the emperor issued an edict asking, "Locusts have plagued us for years, even persisting into winter—what is the cause of this omen?"
units.literal: In the first year of Guanghe an imperial edict posed the question: "Locusts have swarmed year after year, leaping even into winter—where does the blame lie?"

units.zh: 蔡邕对曰：「臣闻《易传》曰：'大作不时，天降灾，厥咎蝗虫来。'《河图秘征篇》曰：'帝贪则政暴而吏酷，酷则诛深必杀，主蝗虫。'蝗虫，贪苛之所致也。」
units.en: Cai Yong answered: "The Tradition of the Changes teaches that untimely public works bring Heaven's scourge in the form of locusts. The River Chart adds that imperial greed breeds cruel officials whose endless killing draws the locust plague. Swarms, in short, follow rapacious rule."
units.literal: Cai Yong replied: "Your servant has heard the Tradition of the Changes say: 'Great works done out of season—Heaven sends disaster; the blame is that locusts come.' The Secret Signs Chapter of the River Chart says: 'When the emperor is greedy, government grows violent and officials cruel; when cruelty deepens, executions are sure to follow—locusts are the omen.' Locusts are caused by greed and harsh exaction."

units.zh: 是时，百官迁徙，皆私上礼西园以为府。
units.en: Just then, as offices were reshuffled, officials were secretly currying favor at the Western Garden, turning it into a personal power base.
units.literal: At that time the hundred officials were being transferred, and all privately presented gifts at the Western Garden to make it their headquarters.

units.zh: 献帝兴平元年夏，大蝗。
units.en: Xingping 1 (194 CE), summer: locusts blotted out the sky.
units.literal: In the summer of the first year of Xingping, Emperor Xian, great locusts.

units.zh: 是时，天下大乱。
units.en: The realm was already torn by warlord strife.
units.literal: At that time all under Heaven was in great chaos.

units.zh: 建安二年五月，蝗。
units.en: Jian'an 2 (197 CE), fifth month: the hoppers returned.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Jian'an: locusts.
